intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in one of nature's most spectacular events. Join a guided game drive to observe predator-prey interactions, big cats, and diverse wildlife in their natural habitat across the vast savannah plains.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Explore Amboseli National Park, home to some of Africa's largest elephant herds set against the iconic backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Take a guided game drive to observe elephants, lions, cheetahs, and over 400 bird species while enjoying breathtaking views of Africa's highest peak across the border.

experiences.name: Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate National Park
experiences.description: Embark on a rare walking and cycling safari through Hell's Gate, one of the few Kenyan parks where you can explore on foot without a vehicle. Trek through dramatic gorges, geothermal hot springs, and towering volcanic cliffs while spotting zebras, giraffes, and buffalo up close in a truly immersive nature experience.

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Rhino Safari
experiences.description: Visit the alkaline Lake Nakuru, famous for its stunning flocks of pink flamingos that paint the shoreline in vivid color. The national park is also a critical sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, as well as leopards, lions, and Rothschild giraffes, making it one of Kenya's most rewarding and compact wildlife destinations.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village Experience and Bush Dinner
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the rich traditions of the Maasai people with an authentic village visit near the Mara. Participate in traditional dances, learn about ancient warrior customs, visit local homesteads, and enjoy a memorable bush dinner under the stars surrounded by the sounds of the African wilderness — a perfect blend of culture and nature.
experiences.location: Maasai Villages, Narok County near Maasai Mara

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked airport transfer or use a reputable taxi to reach Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack from the airport kiosk or a 24-hour convenience store near the hotel on arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to save money and avoid overcharging. Keep small Kenyan shillings handy for tips. The resort is beachfront so enjoy the sound of the ocean as you settle in.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a late breakfast, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get oriented. Explore the local shoreline and enjoy the warm 25°C weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local market or town center to exchange currency at a bank or licensed forex bureau for the best rates. Pick up a local SIM card for affordable data. Browse local craft stalls and get a feel for the area.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront at sunset. Enjoy the scenic views and relax after your journey. Head back to the resort area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a nearby budget café — try mandazi (Kenyan fried dough) and chai tea for an authentic and affordable start (approx. KES 200-400)
meals.lunch: Local 'mama mboga' street food stall — rice, beans, and sukuma wiki (collard greens) for a filling and cheap meal (approx. KES 150-300)
meals.dinner: Affordable local restaurant near the beachfront — try nyama choma (grilled meat) or grilled fish with ugali (approx. KES 500-800)

day_by_day.notes: July is dry season in Kenya with only about 30mm of rain expected — great weather for outdoor exploration. Apply sunscreen as the coastal sun can be strong even at 25°C.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk along the coastal vegetation near the resort. Kenya's coast is rich in bird species including kingfishers, sunbirds, and herons. Bring binoculars if available or rent a pair locally.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby nature reserve or coastal forest for a self-guided or budget group nature walk. Look for vervet monkeys, bush babies, and coastal wildlife. Many community-run reserves offer entry at KES 300-600.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a sunset view from the beachfront. Explore the local evening market for fresh tropical fruits and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit plate and chai at a local roadside stall (approx. KES 200-350)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from local market produce — bananas, groundnuts, and chapati (approx. KES 200-300)
meals.dinner: Budget seafood dinner at a local beach restaurant — grilled tilapia or prawns with coconut rice (approx. KES 600-900)

day_by_day.notes: Start birdwatching early (6:00-8:00 AM) when birds are most active. Wear neutral-colored clothing to avoid startling wildlife. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for a full-day budget safari day trip to a nearby national park or game reserve. Many operators offer shared group safari vehicles at significantly reduced rates compared to private tours. Look for community conservancy options.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the safari game drive through the savannah. Look for the Big Five — lion, elephant, buffalo, leopard, and rhino. July is excellent for wildlife viewing as animals gather around water sources during the dry season.
day_by_day.evening: Return from the safari by late afternoon/early evening. Rest and freshen up at the resort. Share safari photos and stories.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — porridge or eggs and toast (approx. KES 300-500)
meals.lunch: Pack a budget lunch box from the resort or local deli before departure — sandwiches, fruit, and water (approx. KES 300-400)
meals.dinner: Celebrate your first safari day at a local restaurant with a hearty meal — beef stew with ugali and kachumbari salad (approx. KES 500-700)

day_by_day.notes: Book shared safari vehicles at least 2-3 days in advance through local budget operators or hostel noticeboards. Bring a light jacket as early morning game drives can be cool. July is peak dry season — excellent visibility and wildlife concentration near water holes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local community conservation project or wildlife sanctuary in the morning. Many offer guided walks at affordable community rates (KES 500-1000) with knowledgeable local guides who share insights on Kenyan ecosystems and conservation efforts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby nature trail or coastal mangrove forest. Mangroves are vital ecosystems and home to unique bird species, crabs, and marine life. Budget guided mangrove tours are available through local eco-tourism groups.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a cultural evening at a local community center or village — traditional Kenyan music, dance, and storytelling. Many community groups offer these experiences as cultural tourism at low cost (KES 300-600).

meals.breakfast: Local café breakfast — mahamri (coconut doughnuts) and spiced tea (approx. KES 200-350)
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut water and grilled corn from a roadside vendor, plus a samosa or two (approx. KES 150-250)
meals.dinner: Community-run restaurant or home-hosted dinner experience — pilau rice, chicken curry, and kachumbari (approx. KES 500-800)

day_by_day.notes: Supporting community conservation projects directly benefits local wildlife protection efforts. Carry insect repellent for mangrove walks. Respect local cultural customs during the evening cultural experience — ask before photographing people.

day_by_day.morning: Second safari day trip — explore a different game reserve or a section of the park not visited on Day 4. Focus on smaller wildlife and ecosystems — reptiles, insects, and plant life that are often overlooked on standard game drives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local watering hole or salt lick in the afternoon — this is when large mammals like elephants and zebras are most active. Spend time observing animal behavior and interactions in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner moment at a scenic viewpoint — watch the African sunset paint the sky in shades of orange and red. This is a quintessential Kenya experience that costs nothing but is absolutely priceless.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from the resort — boiled eggs, bread, and juice (approx. KES 250-400)
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch near the game reserve — local packed lunch with chapati, vegetables, and fruit (approx. KES 300-450)
meals.dinner: Beachfront dinner at a budget restaurant — whole grilled fish with coconut sauce and rice (approx. KES 600-900)

day_by_day.notes: Afternoon game drives (3:00-6:00 PM) are often the best for big cat sightings as lions and leopards become active. Carry a zoom lens or binoculars for distant wildlife observation. Stay inside the vehicle at all times during game drives.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day morning — enjoy a slow breakfast and a swim at the beachfront. Take time to write travel notes, organize photos, and plan the remaining days. The warm 25°C weather is perfect for relaxing by the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local coastal town on foot or by tuk-tuk (very affordable at KES 50-150 per ride). Visit a local museum or cultural heritage site to learn about Kenyan coastal history, Swahili culture, and the Mijikenda people.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local beach volleyball game or community sports event. Kenyans are very welcoming and love sharing their culture with visitors. End the evening with a walk along the moonlit beach.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or nearby café — fresh fruit salad, yogurt, and tea (approx. KES 300-500)
meals.lunch: Local food court or market stall — biryani rice with chicken or vegetables (approx. KES 300-500)
meals.dinner: Try a local Swahili cuisine restaurant — mtuzi wa samaki (fish curry) with coconut rice and kachumbari (approx. KES 500-800)

day_by_day.notes: Tuk-tuks are a fun and budget-friendly way to get around coastal towns. Always agree on the fare before getting in. July evenings are pleasant with a light coastal breeze — perfect for beach walks.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning nature photography walk along the coastline and surrounding vegetation. The golden morning light is perfect for capturing wildlife, landscapes, and local life. Look for shore birds, crabs, and coastal plants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local snake park or wildlife rescue center if available in the region. These facilities often charge minimal entry fees and provide fascinating education about Kenya's reptiles and rescued wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local guided night walk or nocturnal wildlife tour — spot bush babies, nightjars, and other nocturnal creatures. Many community guides offer this experience at budget rates (KES 500-800 per person).

meals.breakfast: Street food breakfast — mkate wa ufuta (sesame bread) with avocado and tea (approx. KES 200-350)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack — fresh mango, roasted groundnuts, and sugarcane juice (approx. KES 150-250)
meals.dinner: Local nyama choma joint — grilled goat or beef with mukimo (mashed potatoes with greens) and a cold Tusker beer (approx. KES 600-900)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a red-light torch for the night walk to avoid disturbing nocturnal animals. Night walks must always be done with an experienced local guide for safety. The dry July weather means clear skies — excellent for stargazing after the night walk.

day_by_day.morning: Final full safari experience — book a dawn game drive starting at 5:30 AM for the best chance of seeing predators returning from overnight hunts. This is considered the golden hour of African wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from the game drive, visit a local craft market to purchase budget-friendly souvenirs — wooden carvings, Maasai beadwork, kikoi fabric, and local art. Practice bargaining respectfully for fair prices.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and reflection evening. Take a final sunset walk along the beachfront of Aegean Bliss Resort. Reflect on the incredible wildlife and nature experiences of the past 10 days.

meals.breakfast: Very early pre-dawn snack before game drive — energy bars, bananas, and thermos coffee (approx. KES 150-250)
meals.lunch: Celebratory lunch at a slightly nicer local restaurant — treat yourself to a full Kenyan spread within budget (approx. KES 700-1000)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the resort restaurant or a recommended local spot — seafood platter with Swahili spices and coconut dessert (approx. KES 800-1200)

day_by_day.notes: Dawn game drives require early wake-up (4:30-5:00 AM). Layer up as early mornings can be surprisingly cool even in July. When buying souvenirs, support local artisans directly rather than large commercial shops. Keep some budget aside for tips for guides, drivers, and resort staff.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a last breakfast with ocean views. Take a final short walk along the beach to collect memories (and perhaps a few shells). Pack and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort. Depending on flight time, arrange a final tuk-tuk or taxi tour of the local area or simply relax at a café near the airport with a final cup of Kenyan chai and mandazi.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for departure. Allow extra time for check-in and security. Carry any remaining Kenyan snacks — dried mango, macadamia nuts, and Kenyan tea — as gifts or personal treats for the journey home.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy a full spread to fuel the travel day (approx. KES 400-600)
meals.lunch: Airport café or nearby eatery — light meal before departure (approx. KES 400-700)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Declare any wildlife products or plant material at customs — purchasing protected species products is illegal. Kenyan macadamia nuts, coffee, and tea make excellent legal and affordable souvenirs. Keep a small amount of KES for airport tips and last-minute needs.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack or room service at Aegean Bliss Resort if available upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance to avoid delays at night. Keep essentials in your carry-on for easy access. Exchange a small amount of currency (Kenyan Shillings) at the airport for tips and incidentals.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a relaxed orientation walk along the beachfront to get acquainted with the surroundings, breathe in the coastal air, and recover from jet lag. Visit the resort's amenities and plan ahead with the concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area near the resort. Visit a nearby nature trail or coastal viewpoint. Take a gentle introductory nature walk to spot local birdlife and coastal flora — a perfect low-key start to your Kenyan adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset from the beachfront. Head to a local mid-range restaurant near the resort for a welcome dinner featuring traditional Kenyan coastal cuisine such as grilled fish, ugali, and sukuma wiki.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or at the resort's restaurant
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the resort's beach café — try nyama choma (grilled meat) or a fresh salad
meals.dinner: Dinner at a nearby local restaurant — recommended: Swahili-style grilled fish with coconut rice, budget around KES 1,500–2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to rest and acclimatize. Confirm all upcoming safari bookings with the concierge. Apply sunscreen — July sun in Kenya can be deceptively strong. Warm summer weather expected with highs around 25°C.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure after breakfast for a full-day excursion to Hell's Gate National Park. Begin with the Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate — one of Kenya's few parks where you can walk and cycle freely among wildlife. Explore the dramatic gorges, geothermal steam vents, and towering cliffs while spotting zebras, buffaloes, giraffes, and raptors up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Hell's Gate experience with a cycling safari through the park's open savannah. Visit Fischer's Tower and the Central Tower — iconic rock formations. Descend into Ol Njorowa Gorge for a guided walk through the narrow canyon with a local ranger.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort or a nearby eatery. Share stories from the day's adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — pack energy snacks for the safari
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch inside Hell's Gate National Park — arrange with the resort the evening before
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant — try Kenyan beef stew with chapati or pilau rice, budget around KES 1,500–2,000

day_by_day.notes: Hell's Gate is approximately 1.5–2 hours from Nairobi area. Wear comfortable walking shoes and light breathable clothing. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and a light jacket for the gorge. Bicycle hire is available at the park gate for around KES 600–800.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure for Lake Nakuru National Park for the Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Rhino Safari. Arrive in time for the golden morning light — ideal for photography. Witness thousands of pink flamingos painting the alkaline lake shoreline in breathtaking color.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive around Lake Nakuru. Search for the park's famous white and black rhinos — one of Kenya's key rhino sanctuaries. Also look out for leopards in the acacia trees, lions, Rothschild's giraffes, and waterbucks. Enjoy a lakeside picnic lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort, arriving by early evening. Freshen up and enjoy a quiet dinner. Reflect on the incredible wildlife sightings of the day.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at a designated picnic site inside Lake Nakuru National Park — arrange packed lunch with resort
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant near the resort or resort dining — try tilapia fish with kachumbari salad, budget KES 1,500–2,500

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru is roughly 2 hours from Nairobi. July is dry season making flamingo and wildlife viewing excellent. Bring binoculars and a camera with a zoom lens. Park entry fees: approximately USD 60 per adult. Book a reliable safari vehicle and driver-guide in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Maasai Mara — the highlight of the trip. It's a 5–6 hour drive or a 45-minute scenic charter flight from Nairobi (budget-friendly option: shared shuttle or self-drive). Check into a mid-range tented camp in the Mara ecosystem. After settling in, enjoy an afternoon game drive.
day_by_day.afternoon: First game drive in the Maasai Mara — begin the Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari experience. July is peak migration season: witness vast herds of wildebeest, zebras, and Thomson's gazelles moving across the plains. Spot the Big Five and enjoy the raw, unfiltered African wilderness.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for sundowner drinks on the savannah. Enjoy a bush dinner under the stars at the tented camp — a magical Maasai Mara evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure or en route
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the tented camp upon arrival in the Mara
meals.dinner: Bush dinner at the tented camp — included in most mid-range Mara camp packages; expect grilled meats, vegetables, and stargazing

day_by_day.notes: Book your Mara tented camp well in advance — July is peak season. Mid-range options include camps like Mara Serena, Keekorok Lodge, or Basecamp Masai Mara at approximately USD 150–250 per night full board. Bring warm layers for early morning and evening drives — temperatures drop significantly.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a sunrise game drive in the Maasai Mara. This is the best time to witness predator activity — lions on the hunt, cheetahs scanning the plains, and hyenas returning from nocturnal foraging. Watch the golden savannah light up at sunrise over the Mara River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full-day game drive with a focus on the Great Migration. Position near the Mara River crossing points to witness the dramatic — and potentially life-or-death — wildebeest river crossings with Nile crocodiles lying in wait. This is one of nature's greatest spectacles.
day_by_day.evening: Participate in the Maasai Cultural Village Experience and Bush Dinner. Visit an authentic Maasai village near the Mara, meet the community, learn about traditional customs, watch ceremonial dances, and enjoy a memorable bush dinner around a campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast or flask of tea/coffee from camp before dawn drive
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch on the plains — arranged by your camp and served in the field
meals.dinner: Traditional Maasai bush dinner as part of the cultural village experience — included in the activity package

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai Cultural Village experience costs approximately USD 30–50 per person. Respect cultural norms — ask permission before photographing community members. The river crossing viewings are unpredictable — patience is key. Stay in the vehicle at all times during game drives.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning game drive in the Maasai Mara — explore the quieter northern conservancies bordering the main reserve for a more exclusive wildlife experience with fewer vehicles. Look for leopards, wild dogs, and the elusive serval cat in the tall grass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Mara camp and begin the journey toward Amboseli National Park. This is a long transfer (approximately 5–6 hours) — consider an overnight stop or arrange a scenic route through the Rift Valley. Check into a mid-range lodge near Amboseli.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your Amboseli lodge and settle in. Enjoy a relaxing evening with views of Mount Kilimanjaro on the horizon. Dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Mara tented camp before checkout
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at a local restaurant en route — try nyama choma with ugali, budget KES 800–1,200
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Amboseli lodge — expect buffet-style meals with Kenyan and continental options

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Maasai Mara to Amboseli is long — consider breaking the journey or flying between parks for efficiency. Mid-range Amboseli lodges include Ol Tukai Lodge or Kibo Safari Camp at approximately USD 120–200 per night. Confirm bookings in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Amboseli National Park for the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views experience. July mornings offer the clearest views of Mount Kilimanjaro before clouds build. Photograph massive elephant herds moving across the plains with Africa's highest peak as a backdrop — an iconic and unforgettable scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Amboseli — visit the swamps where elephants wade and bathe. Look for lions, cheetahs, hippos, and hundreds of bird species. Visit the Observation Hill for a panoramic view of the park and the Kilimanjaro massif. Enjoy a lakeside picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a sundowner on the terrace with Kilimanjaro views. Enjoy dinner at the lodge and share the day's wildlife highlights with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before the morning drive
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Observation Hill or lodge lunch on return
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner — try Kenyan lamb stew or roasted chicken with local vegetables; budget included in lodge package or KES 2,000–3,000 à la carte

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli's elephant population is one of the most studied in the world. Keep a respectful distance from elephant herds. Morning light before 9 AM gives the best Kilimanjaro photography conditions. Dust can be heavy in Amboseli — protect your camera gear.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise game drive in Amboseli — a last chance to see elephants and predators in the soft morning light. Spend time at the swamp areas where large elephant bulls are often found. Capture final photos of Kilimanjaro before the clouds roll in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Amboseli lodge and begin the drive back toward Nairobi (approximately 4 hours). Stop at a local Maasai market along the route to pick up handcrafted souvenirs — beaded jewelry, wood carvings, and colorful shukas (Maasai blankets).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Aegean Bliss Resort or a Nairobi-area hotel. Enjoy a celebratory farewell dinner at a well-regarded mid-range Nairobi restaurant to mark the end of your safari adventure.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Amboseli lodge before checkout
meals.lunch: Lunch en route at a local roadside eatery or town restaurant — try pilau rice with chicken, budget KES 600–1,000
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a recommended Nairobi mid-range restaurant — try Carnivore Restaurant for a classic Kenyan experience, budget KES 3,000–4,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for the Maasai market stop — bargaining is expected and part of the cultural experience. Start with half the asking price. Confirm your return flight details and arrange airport transfer for the following day if departing on Day 10.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kenya — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and take time to pack, review memories, and write travel notes. If time allows, visit a local nature reserve or the Nairobi National Park for a final wildlife encounter just minutes from the city — the only national park in the world bordering a capital city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a local craft market such as the Maasai Market or Utamaduni Craft Centre. Visit a local café for a final cup of authentic Kenyan single-origin coffee or chai tea. Begin making your way to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Nairobi with incredible memories of Kenya's wildlife, landscapes, and people. Arrive at the airport with ample time for check-in and departure formalities.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort or hotel — savor it!
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the craft market or airport — try a mandazi (Kenyan doughnut) and masala chai, budget KES 400–800
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Declare any wildlife products — it is illegal to export certain animal products from Kenya. Keep your safari photos backed up to cloud storage. Yellow fever vaccination certificate may be required depending on your onward destination.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village Experience and Bush Dinner
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the rich traditions of the Maasai people with an authentic village visit near the Mara. Participate in traditional dances, learn about ancient warrior customs, visit local homesteads, and enjoy a memorable bush dinner under the stars surrounded by the sounds of the African wilderness — a perfect blend of culture and nature.
experiences.location: Maasai Villages, Narok County near Maasai Mara

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Welcome drink and light late-night supper awaits upon check-in. Resort concierge briefs you on the 10-day itinerary.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport lounge
meals.lunch: In-flight or at airport lounge
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome supper at Aegean Bliss Resort — charcuterie board, artisan breads, and a curated selection of Kenyan teas and wines served in your suite

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day only. No sightseeing scheduled. Ensure luggage includes safari-appropriate attire: neutral tones (khaki, olive, beige), light layers for cool mornings, and sturdy walking shoes. Resort butler available 24/7.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort orientation breakfast followed by a guided beachfront nature walk along Kenya's coastline. Spot coastal birdlife, explore mangrove edges, and enjoy the warm Indian Ocean breeze. A private naturalist guide accompanies the 2-hour walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private resort pool and spa afternoon. Indulge in a 90-minute Maasai-inspired body treatment using indigenous herbs and volcanic clay at the resort's luxury spa. Alternatively, enjoy a snorkeling session in the crystal-clear coastal waters with a certified dive master.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's private beach deck. Enjoy a curated sundowner menu featuring Kenyan craft gins, fresh tropical juices, and canapés. Followed by a five-course fine dining dinner at the resort's signature oceanfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the resort's Ocean Terrace Restaurant — fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan chai, eggs Benedict, smoked marlin, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled prawns, avocado salad, and freshly squeezed passion fruit juice
meals.dinner: Five-course tasting menu at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — highlights include Swahili-spiced lobster bisque, pan-seared kingfish, and a passion fruit soufflé with Kenyan vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: Recovery and acclimatization day after long-haul travel. Weather expected: 25°C, warm and sunny. Light linen clothing recommended. SPF 50+ sunscreen advised for coastal activities.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from the coastal airstrip to Amboseli National Park (approximately 1.5 hours). Upon landing, transfer by luxury 4x4 Land Cruiser to your exclusive bush camp for a quick orientation. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views experience — a premium guided game drive through the park's iconic elephant corridors with Africa's largest elephant herds moving against the snow-capped backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Amboseli safari with a post-lunch game drive focusing on predator tracking — lions, cheetahs, and hyenas are frequently spotted in the open plains. Visit the Observation Hill for panoramic views over Amboseli's swamps and the surrounding ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the luxury bush camp. Enjoy a private bush sundowner on the savannah — champagne and canapés served as the sun sets behind Kilimanjaro. Dinner under the stars at a lantern-lit bush dining setup exclusive to your party.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast at the resort before departure — continental spread with Kenyan coffee and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch in the bush — served from wicker hampers including cold cuts, artisan cheeses, fresh salads, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private open-air bush dinner — three courses featuring slow-braised Kenyan lamb, roasted root vegetables, and a dark chocolate fondant with salted caramel

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is one of Africa's premier elephant-watching destinations. July is peak dry season, making wildlife viewing exceptional. Binoculars and camera with telephoto lens strongly recommended. Temperatures can drop to 12°C after sunset — bring a light fleece.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a hot air balloon safari over Amboseli at sunrise (approximately 06:00 launch). Float silently over the vast plains watching elephants, zebras, and wildebeest from above with unobstructed views of Kilimanjaro bathed in golden morning light. Flight lasts approximately 1 hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-balloon champagne breakfast in the bush followed by a guided walking safari with a Maasai ranger — learn to track wildlife on foot, identify animal prints, and understand the ecosystem at ground level. Return to camp for a leisurely afternoon rest and spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer back to Amboseli airstrip for a scenic charter flight back to the coast. Welcome back to Aegean Bliss Resort with a refreshing welcome drink. Relaxed dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory champagne bush breakfast immediately after balloon landing — full cooked spread including eggs, bacon, smoked salmon, and Kenyan honey
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the bush camp — grilled chicken skewers, quinoa salad, and freshly blended tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's beachfront grill — whole grilled Swahili spiced snapper, coconut rice, and mango sorbet

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon must be booked in advance and is weather-dependent. Operator will confirm the morning of. Wear warm layers for the balloon flight as temperatures at altitude are cooler. This is a highlight experience — ensure camera batteries are fully charged.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight from the coast to the Maasai Mara (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Arrive at one of Kenya's most exclusive private conservancies adjacent to the Mara. Check into a luxury tented camp. Begin the Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — a premium full-day game drive to witness millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles in their legendary annual migration across the Mara River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Great Migration experience with a focus on Mara River crossings — position your vehicle at a prime crossing point and witness the dramatic spectacle of thousands of animals braving crocodile-filled waters. Your expert guide provides live commentary and photography tips.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the tented camp for a signature sundowner experience on a private kopje (rocky outcrop) overlooking the Mara plains. Dinner at the camp's open-air dining area with a live Maasai cultural performance.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Bush lunch served in the field — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, and chilled beverages in a shaded acacia grove
meals.dinner: Four-course dinner at the luxury tented camp — wild mushroom soup, Mara-style grilled beef tenderloin with chimichurri, and a warm chocolate brownie with vanilla bean ice cream

day_by_day.notes: July is the absolute peak month for the Great Migration — river crossings are most frequent between July and October. This is a world-class wildlife spectacle. Bring dust covers for camera equipment. Neutral-colored clothing is essential in the Mara.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn game drive in the Maasai Mara conservancy to catch big cats on the hunt at first light. The Mara is home to one of Africa's highest concentrations of lions, leopards, and cheetahs. Your private guide and tracker focus on predator activity in the golden morning hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maasai Cultural Village Experience — visit an authentic Maasai boma (village) near the Mara. Engage with elders and warriors, learn about traditional beadwork, participate in the adamu (jumping dance), and gain insight into centuries-old pastoral traditions. Includes a private guided tour of the village.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive Bush Dinner experience — a private candlelit dinner set up in a scenic location on the Mara plains, complete with a personal chef, sommelier, and butler service under a canopy of stars. Features a curated Kenyan wine and cocktail pairing.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the field after the morning game drive — full hot breakfast with Kenyan coffee and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Traditional Maasai-inspired lunch at the village — roasted meats, fermented milk (for the adventurous), and local vegetables prepared by village women
meals.dinner: Private bush dinner on the Mara plains — five courses featuring Kenyan-inspired cuisine: avocado and crayfish starter, tomato gazpacho, flame-grilled Mara game (where available and ethical), and a Kenyan honey panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai Cultural Village Experience is deeply respectful and community-benefit focused — fees go directly to the village. Photography is welcome with permission. The bush dinner is one of the most memorable experiences of the trip — request a specific setup (e.g., beside a river or under a specific tree) through your camp concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning game drive in the Maasai Mara with a focus on the Big Five checklist — lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino. Your guide will work to complete any remaining sightings. Mid-morning return to camp for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from the Mara to Lake Nakuru (approximately 45 minutes). Check into a luxury lodge overlooking the lake. Begin the Lake Nakuru Flamingo and Rhino Safari — explore the alkaline lake shores where hundreds of thousands of pink flamingos create a breathtaking shoreline spectacle, alongside white and black rhinos in their protected sanctuary.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner game drive around Lake Nakuru's forested escarpment — spot leopards, Rothschild's giraffes (an endangered subspecies), and waterbuck as the light fades. Return to the lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Mara tented camp before departure
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Lake Nakuru lodge upon arrival — Caesar salad, grilled tilapia, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Lake Nakuru lodge's fine dining restaurant — Kenyan lake fish prepared three ways, accompanied by local vegetables and a Kenyan coffee crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a critical rhino sanctuary. Both black and white rhinos can be seen here — one of the best places in Kenya for rhino sightings. The flamingo numbers vary by season but July typically offers excellent viewing. Bring a wide-angle lens for flamingo panoramas.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park focusing on rhino tracking with a specialist ranger. Visit the southern end of the lake for the best flamingo density and birdwatching — over 450 bird species have been recorded here. Photography session at the lake's edge at golden hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Hell's Gate National Park (approximately 1.5 hours from Nakuru). Begin the Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate — one of Kenya's most unique parks where you can walk and cycle freely among wildlife. Explore the dramatic volcanic gorges, geothermal hot springs, and towering cliffs. Spot zebras, buffalos, and eagles on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to a luxury lodge near Hell's Gate. Enjoy a private geothermal spa experience — natural hot spring pools heated by volcanic activity, a uniquely Kenyan wellness experience. Followed by dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Lake Nakuru lodge — fresh fruit, yogurt, eggs to order, and Kenyan black tea
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in Hell's Gate Gorge — served in the dramatic canyon setting with artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Hell's Gate area luxury lodge — wood-fired pizza with Kenyan toppings (caramelized onion, local cheese, and smoked meats), followed by a warm lemon tart

day_by_day.notes: Hell's Gate is the inspiration for the landscapes in Disney's 'The Lion King.' Walking and cycling safaris are rare in Kenya — this is a genuinely unique experience. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for gorge walking. The geothermal spa is a must — book in advance through your lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Private charter flight back to the Kenyan coast (approximately 1.5 hours). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a leisurely mid-morning arrival with welcome refreshments. Spend the morning on a private snorkeling or deep-sea fishing excursion on the Indian Ocean, arranged by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure — choose from the resort's premium offerings: private catamaran sailing along the coast, a guided mangrove kayaking tour, or a full afternoon at the resort's luxury spa with a couples' or solo treatment package including a hot stone massage, facial, and hydrotherapy circuit.
day_by_day.evening: Private beach bonfire dinner — a romantic and exclusive setup on the resort's private stretch of beach. Personal chef prepares a live-fire seafood feast with freshly caught lobster, prawns, and crab. Wine pairing by the resort sommelier. Live acoustic music by a local Kenyan artist.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Hell's Gate lodge before departure — continental spread with local honey and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch aboard the catamaran or at the resort's beach bar — grilled calamari, coconut crab salad, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire seafood feast — whole grilled lobster, spiced prawns, and crab claws with herb butter, accompanied by a curated South African and Kenyan wine selection

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate decompression day between safari activities and the final day. The private beach bonfire dinner is the premium highlight of the coastal stay — confirm the setup with the concierge at least 24 hours in advance. Weather: 25°C, warm and ideal for beach activities.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga session on the resort's private beach deck with a certified instructor — a serene farewell to Kenya's coastline. Followed by a leisurely farewell breakfast with views of the Indian Ocean. Time for last-minute souvenir shopping at the resort's curated boutique featuring authentic Kenyan crafts, Maasai jewelry, and locally sourced coffee and teas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-out from Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Mombasa Moi International Airport or Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport depending on departure flight routing. Airport lounge access arranged for a comfortable pre-departure experience.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kenya. Farewell gift from the resort — a curated Kenyan hamper including single-origin Kenyan coffee, Maasai beaded bracelet, and a handwritten note from the resort team.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort's Ocean Terrace — full à la carte spread: smoked salmon eggs Benedict, tropical fruit platters, Kenyan chai, freshly squeezed juices, and a selection of pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport lounge or en route — finger sandwiches, salads, and soft drinks
meals.dinner: In-flight or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight timing with the concierge to ensure the transfer is scheduled correctly — allow at least 3 hours before departure. Kenya has a 30 kg checked baggage allowance on most international routes. Declare any wildlife products (e.g., certain shells or animal products) at customs — resort boutique items are all ethically sourced and legally exportable. A truly world-class 10-day Kenyan luxury experience concludes today.
